messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: streaming-p99 > 1.2s across eu-west2 + us-east-1 for 6m — SLO breach (p99). Affected: real-time streaming endpoints (consumer sessions). Detect: increased TLS handshake times, SYN retransmits, and DNS timeouts on cross-zone egress paths.

sara (oncall): ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics & traces now. which clusters are most impacted? :eyes:

kim (netops): eu-west2-a/b showing biggest spike. I'm seeing conntrack table near saturation on NAT nodes and elevated TCP retransmits between azB->azC. DNS latencies also spiking for upstream resolvers in eu-west2.

mike (infra): +1. Looking at autoscale for nat-agent group and load balancer health. Rolling a probe to see if we have ephemeral port exhaustion.

sara (oncall): quick checks: 
- streaming gateway p95 stable ~120ms but p99 jumps to 1.2-1.6s
- tail stalls concentrated on long-lived streaming sessions (~>60s)
- logs show repeated TLS handshake retries from clients behind same NAT IPs

sara (oncall): running conntrack dumps on one NAT node: ``conntrack -L | wc -l`` -> 175k entries (table size 200k). Reuse high.

kim (netops): paste from tcpdump on nat-egress-03: 
```
12:03:21.123456 IP client->service: SYN
12:03:21.223789 IP client->service: SYN retransmit
12:03:23.334567 IP client->service: SYN retransmit
```
lots of retransmits and RTT jitter.

mike (infra): mitigation plan: 
1) scale NAT pool: increase nat instances + bump conntrack_max via sysctl on NAT nodes
2) temporarily reroute streaming egress via backup NAT cluster in eu-west1 to offload
3) add short-term DNS fallback to alternative resolvers to avoid single-resolver stalls

kim (netops): I'll implement routing change (BGP/eBPF policy) to steer a percentage of streaming egress to eu-west1 NATs. Doing a 20% trial then ramp if stable.

sara (oncall): mike, can you cherry-pick a sysctl change and rollout to one nat node to validate? e.g. ``sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000`` then `conntrack -L` to validate.

mike (infra): applying to nat-egress-03 now via ssh. Patch: ``sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000`` -> applied. conntrack count still ~178k but headroom increased.

deploy-bot: routing-change: initiated by kim (netops) — rollout id r-2026-031. Steady-state target: 20% streaming egress -> eu-west1-nat-cluster.

kim (netops): routing change live for 20% at 12:08 UTC. Monitoring p99 and retransmit rate.

sara (oncall): visible improvements within 3m: eu-west2 p99 dropping from 1.5s -> 800-900ms. streaming tail stalls reduced but still occasional spikes.

mike (infra): scaling nat pool +1 instance in eu-west2 done (terraform apply completed). Also increased ephemeral port range on NATs: ``sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'``

kim (netops): DNS fallback configured for streaming-gateway to use secondary resolver list. We saw a 20% reduction in DNS timeouts.

sara (oncall): confirming customer impact: traffic affecting ~2.3% of active streaming sessions (sessions with >50ms handshake retries). Some customers reported degraded streaming startup times. No data loss reported.

alex (sre): joining for handoff. summary for night: 
- root cause hypothesis: NAT/egress path saturation + intermittent DNS timeouts causing prolonged TLS handshake retries and SYN retransmits -> tail latency hit on streaming sessions.
- mitigations applied: conntrack_max bump, increased ephemeral ports, +1 NAT instance, 20% egress reroute to eu-west1, DNS fallback enabled.
- observed outcome: p99 improved ~40-60% from peak, p95 unchanged. streaming stalls reduced but not fully back to baseline.

sara (oncall): I'll continue 15m of active monitoring. If p99 remains >800ms we'll escalate to full region failover (route 100% to eu-west1) and open customer comms.

kim (netops): telemetry: retransmit rate dropped from 4.2% -> 1.1% after reroute/scale. conntrack utilization now ~62%.

mike (infra): leaving a short runbook snippet: 
```
- If conntrack > 75%: add NAT instance, bump conntrack_max by +50k, expand ip_local_port_range
- If TLS handshake p99 still >1s after scale: trigger full egress reroute to eu-west1
- If retransmits persist: run tcpdump on nat nodes and escalate to networkfabric team
```

sara (oncall): starting gradual rollback of 20% trial in 30m if stable. Otherwise escalate. updating incident doc.

alex (sre): taking the handoff at 12:26 UTC. I'll stay on until 02:00 UTC and will notify if any regression. Running scheduled checks: p99, conntrack, retransmit rate, DNS error rate.

sara (oncall): thanks team. sending short customer impact note to support to craft comms: "intermittent streaming startup latency for small subset of sessions; mitigations applied; monitoring."

deploy-bot: routing-change: monitoring OK. r-2026-031 at 12:08 -> 20% -> stable.

alex (sre): quick note: saved artifacts -> `tcpdump_eu-west2-12-03.pcap`, `conntrack_dump_nat-egress-03.log`, grafana_snapshot_4623456000.png. Adding to incident ticket.

kim (netops): leaving a tip — consider separate egress pool for long-lived streaming flows in future to avoid NAT churn mixing ephemeral web flows and streaming.

alex (sre): agreed. adding to action items: design dedicated streaming egress subnet + capacity reservation.

sara (oncall): handoff complete. last check: p99 ~720-850ms, retransmit rate 1.0%, conntrack 60-65%. I'll sign off from active paging. Alex takes watch. :white_check_mark:
